```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 7)
```

Three quantities summarise most of what the SIR model says about an outbreak.

* **Basic reproduction number:** $R_0 = \beta/\gamma$. An outbreak can take
  off only if $R_0 > 1$.
* **Herd immunity threshold:** the fraction of the population that must be
  immune so that $R_0 \times (\text{fraction susceptible}) \le 1$, i.e.
  $1 - 1/R_0$.
* **Final size:** the fraction $z$ of the population ever infected, which
  solves $z = 1 - e^{-R_0 z}$ (when almost everyone starts susceptible).

```{r}
beta <- 0.5
gamma <- 0.2
R0 <- beta / gamma
herd_immunity <- 1 - 1 / R0
c(R0 = R0, herd_immunity_threshold = herd_immunity)
```

# Solving for the final size

The final-size equation has no closed-form solution, so we find its root
numerically with `uniroot()`.

```{r}
final_size <- function(R0) {
  if (R0 <= 1) return(0)                       # no major outbreak
  uniroot(function(z) z - (1 - exp(-R0 * z)),
          lower = 1e-6, upper = 1)$root
}

final_size(R0)
```

# Check against the simulated epidemic

```{r}
library(deSolve)
sir <- function(time, state, parms) {
  with(as.list(c(state, parms)), {
    dS <- -beta * S * I / N
    dI <-  beta * S * I / N - gamma * I
    dR <-  gamma * I
    list(c(dS, dI, dR))
  })
}
N <- 1000
out <- as.data.frame(ode(c(S = N - 1, I = 1, R = 0), seq(0, 300, by = 1),
                         sir, c(beta = beta, gamma = gamma, N = N)))
tail(out$R, 1) / N            # fraction ever infected in the simulation
```

The simulation and the equation agree.

# How the final size depends on R0

```{r}
R0_values <- c(1.2, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4)
table_out <- data.frame(
  R0 = R0_values,
  herd_immunity = round(1 - 1 / R0_values, 3),
  final_size = round(sapply(R0_values, final_size), 3)
)
table_out
```

```{r}
curve_R0 <- seq(1.05, 5, by = 0.05)
plot(curve_R0, sapply(curve_R0, final_size), type = "l", lwd = 2,
     xlab = "R0", ylab = "Fraction ever infected",
     main = "Final epidemic size")
lines(curve_R0, 1 - 1 / curve_R0, lty = 2)
legend("bottomright", c("Final size", "Herd immunity threshold"), lty = c(1, 2))
```

Notice that the final size is always larger than the herd immunity threshold:
the epidemic overshoots because infections continue while $I$ is still large.
